raw: Act 1, Scene 2 — A Street

sentences.en: A Street
sentences.ko: 거리

summary.en: Paris asks Capulet if he can marry Juliet. Capulet invites him to a party. By chance, Romeo learns that Rosaline will be at the party too.
summary.ko: 패리스가 캐퓰릿에게 줄리엣과 결혼하게 해 달라고 청한다. 캐퓰릿은 그를 잔치에 초대한다. 로미오는 우연히 로잘린도 그 잔치에 온다는 것을 알게 된다.

raw: Enter Capulet, Paris and Servant.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
But Montague is bound as well as I,
In penalty alike; and ’tis not hard, I think,
For men so old as we to keep the peace.

sentences.en: But Montague is bound by the same penalty as I am.
sentences.ko: 하지만 몬태규도 나와 똑같은 처벌을 받게 되어 있어요.

sentences.en: I think it is not hard for men our age to keep the peace.
sentences.ko: 우리 나이의 사람들이 평화를 유지하는 게 그리 어렵지 않다고 생각해요.

speaker: PARIS
raw:
Of honourable reckoning are you both,
And pity ’tis you liv’d at odds so long.
But now my lord, what say you to my suit?

sentences.en: You are both highly respected men.
sentences.ko: 두 분 모두 존경받는 분들이시군요.

sentences.en: It is a pity that you fought for so long.
sentences.ko: 그토록 오랫동안 싸우셨다니 안타까운 일입니다.

sentences.en: But now, my lord, what do you say to my request?
sentences.ko: 그런데 어르신, 제 청혼은 어떻게 생각하시나요?

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
But saying o’er what I have said before.
My child is yet a stranger in the world,
She hath not seen the change of fourteen years;
Let two more summers wither in their pride
Ere we may think her ripe to be a bride.

sentences.en: I am only repeating what I said before.
sentences.ko: 나는 그저 전에 했던 말을 되풀이할 뿐이에요.

sentences.en: My child is still new to the world.
sentences.ko: 제 아이는 아직 세상이 낯설어요.

sentences.en: She has not seen fourteen years pass.
sentences.ko: 아직 열네 살이 지나지 않았거든요.

sentences.en: Let two more summers pass.
sentences.ko: 두 번의 여름이 더 지나길 기다려 주세요.

sentences.en: Then we can think she is ready to be a bride.
sentences.ko: 그때가 되면 신부가 될 준비가 되었다고 생각할 수 있어요.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Younger than she are happy mothers made.

sentences.en: Girls younger than her are already happy mothers.
sentences.ko: 따님보다 어린 소녀들도 벌써 행복한 어머니가 되었어요.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
And too soon marr’d are those so early made.
The earth hath swallowed all my hopes but she,
She is the hopeful lady of my earth:
But woo her, gentle Paris, get her heart,
My will to her consent is but a part;
And she agree, within her scope of choice
Lies my consent and fair according voice.
This night I hold an old accustom’d feast,
Whereto I have invited many a guest,
Such as I love, and you among the store,
One more, most welcome, makes my number more.
At my poor house look to behold this night
Earth-treading stars that make dark heaven light:
Such comfort as do lusty young men feel
When well apparell’d April on the heel
Of limping winter treads, even such delight
Among fresh female buds shall you this night
Inherit at my house. Hear all, all see,
And like her most whose merit most shall be:
Which, on more view of many, mine, being one,
May stand in number, though in reckoning none.
Come, go with me. Go, sirrah, trudge about
Through fair Verona; find those persons out
Whose names are written there,

sentences.en: Those who marry too early are often unhappy.
sentences.ko: 너무 일찍 결혼하는 사람들은 종종 불행해지곤 해요.

sentences.en: The earth has taken all my hopes except for her.
sentences.ko: 땅이 그 아이만 남기고 내 희망을 모두 삼켜 버렸어요.

sentences.en: She is the only hope I have left in this world.
sentences.ko: 그 아이가 이 세상에 남은 내 유일한 희망이에요.

sentences.en: But try to win her love, gentle Paris.
sentences.ko: 하지만 그 아이의 사랑을 얻으려 애써 보세요, 패리스 백작.

sentences.en: Win her heart.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 마음을 얻으세요.

sentences.en: My wishes matter less than her own consent.
sentences.ko: 제 바람보다 그녀의 동의가 더 중요합니다.

sentences.en: If she agrees, I will gladly agree with her choice.
sentences.ko: 그녀가 동의한다면, 저도 기꺼이 그녀의 선택을 따를 거예요.

sentences.en: I am holding an old traditional feast tonight.
sentences.ko: 오늘 밤 저는 오래된 전통적인 잔치를 열어요.

sentences.en: I have invited many guests to it.
sentences.ko: 많은 손님을 초대했답니다.

sentences.en: I like them all, and you are among them.
sentences.ko: 나는 그들 모두를 좋아하는데, 백작도 그중 한 사람이에요.

sentences.en: One more welcome guest makes my group even better.
sentences.ko: 한 명의 손님이 더 온다면 제 모임은 더욱 완벽해질 거예요.

sentences.en: At my house tonight, look for girls like stars walking on earth, lighting up the dark sky.
sentences.ko: 오늘 밤 제 집에서, 어두운 하늘을 밝히며 땅 위를 걷는 별 같은 소녀들을 보게 될 거예요.

sentences.en: Young men feel great joy when beautiful April follows winter.
sentences.ko: 겨울 뒤에 아름다운 4월이 찾아오면 젊은이들은 큰 기쁨을 느끼죠.

sentences.en: You will find a similar delight with young women at my house tonight.
sentences.ko: 오늘 밤 제 집의 젊은 여성들과도 비슷한 기쁨을 느끼게 될 거예요.

sentences.en: Hear all and see all.
sentences.ko: 모두 듣고 모두 보세요.

sentences.en: Choose the one whose merit is greatest.
sentences.ko: 가장 훌륭한 자질을 가진 사람을 선택하세요.

sentences.en: After you see many girls, my daughter will be just one of them.
sentences.ko: 많은 아가씨를 보고 나면, 내 딸은 그중 하나일 뿐이겠지요.

sentences.en: She may not stand out among them.
sentences.ko: 그녀가 특별히 눈에 띄지 않을 수도 있어요.

sentences.en: Come, go with me.
sentences.ko: 자, 나와 함께 가요.

sentences.en: Go, you there, walk through beautiful Verona.
sentences.ko: 이봐, 아름다운 베로나를 돌아다녀라.

sentences.en: Find the people whose names are written here.
sentences.ko: 여기 이름이 적힌 사람들을 찾아라.

raw: gives a paper

sentences.en: Capulet gives the servant a paper.
sentences.ko: 캐퓰릿이 하인에게 종이를 건넨다.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
and to them say,
My house and welcome on their pleasure stay.

sentences.en: Tell them that my house is open and they are welcome to come.
sentences.ko: 우리 집 문은 열려 있으니 기꺼이 오라고 전해라.

raw: Exeunt Capulet and Paris.

speaker: SERVANT
raw:
Find them out whose names are written here! It is written that the
shoemaker should meddle with his yard and the tailor with his last, the
fisher with his pencil, and the painter with his nets; but I am sent to
find those persons whose names are here writ, and can never find what
names the writing person hath here writ. I must to the learned. In good
time!

sentences.en: Find the people whose names are written here!
sentences.ko: 여기에 적힌 이름의 사람들을 찾아라!

sentences.en: It says that the shoemaker should work with his yard.
sentences.ko: 구두장이는 줄자를 가지고 일해야 한다고 적혀 있다.

sentences.en: The tailor should work with his last.
sentences.ko: 재봉사는 구두 골을 가지고 일해야 하고.

sentences.en: The fisher should work with his pencil.
sentences.ko: 어부는 붓을 가지고 일해야 하고.

sentences.en: And the painter should work with his nets.
sentences.ko: 화가는 그물을 가지고 일해야 한다.

sentences.en: But I am sent to find the people whose names are here.
sentences.ko: 하지만 나는 여기에 이름이 적힌 사람들을 찾으러 왔다.

sentences.en: I cannot know what names the writer put here.
sentences.ko: 글쓴이가 여기에 무슨 이름을 적었는지 나는 알 수가 없다.

sentences.en: I must go to the learned person.
sentences.ko: 글을 아는 사람에게 가야겠다.

sentences.en: Here comes someone just in time!
sentences.ko: 마침 딱 맞춰 누군가 온다!

raw: Enter Benvolio and Romeo.

speaker: BENVOLIO

sentences.en: Listen, man.
sentences.ko: 잘 들어, 친구.

sentences.en: One fire puts out another's burning.
sentences.ko: 하나의 불이 다른 불을 끄기도 해.

sentences.en: One pain is lessened by another's suffering.
sentences.ko: 한 고통은 다른 고통으로 덜어지는 법이야.

sentences.en: If you are dizzy from turning, turning the other way will help.
sentences.ko: 빙글 돌아서 어지럽다면 반대쪽으로 돌면 도움이 돼.

sentences.en: One deep sadness can be cured with another's misery.
sentences.ko: 깊은 슬픔은 다른 슬픔으로 낫기도 하지.

sentences.en: Get a new sickness in your eye.
sentences.ko: 네 눈에 새로운 병을 옮겨 봐.

sentences.en: Then the old poison will die.
sentences.ko: 그러면 오래된 독이 사라질 거야.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Your plantain leaf is excellent for that.

sentences.en: Your plantain leaf is excellent for that.
sentences.ko: 그런 데는 네 질경이 잎이 아주 좋지.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: For what, I pray thee?

sentences.en: For what, may I ask?
sentences.ko: 무엇에 좋다는 거야?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: For your broken shin.

sentences.en: For your broken shin.
sentences.ko: 네 까진 정강이에.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Why, Romeo, art thou mad?

sentences.en: Why, Romeo, are you mad?
sentences.ko: 로미오, 미쳤어?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Not mad, but bound more than a madman is:
Shut up in prison, kept without my food,
Whipp’d and tormented and—God-den, good fellow.

sentences.en: I am not mad, but I am bound more than a madman is.
sentences.ko: 난 미친 게 아니야, 하지만 미친 사람보다 더한 속박에 묶여 있어.

sentences.en: I am locked in prison without my food, whipped and tormented and—good evening, good fellow.
sentences.ko: 먹지도 못한 채 감옥에 갇혀 매 맞고 고문당하고—안녕하시오, 친구.

speaker: SERVANT
raw: God gi’ go-den. I pray, sir, can you read?

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.ko: 안녕하십니까.

sentences.en: Please, sir, can you read?
sentences.ko: 실례지만, 글을 읽으실 수 있습니까?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Ay, mine own fortune in my misery.

sentences.en: Yes, I can read my own fortune in my misery.
sentences.ko: 그래, 내 비참한 운명 정도는 읽을 수 있어.

speaker: SERVANT
raw:
Perhaps you have learned it without book.
But I pray, can you read anything you see?

sentences.en: Perhaps you learned it without a book.
sentences.ko: 책 없이 배우셨을지도 모르겠습니다.

sentences.en: But I ask, can you read anything you see?
sentences.ko: 하지만 묻겠습니다, 눈에 보이는 건 무엇이든 읽으실 수 있습니까?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Ay, If I know the letters and the language.

sentences.en: Yes, if I know the letters and the language.
sentences.ko: 그래, 글자와 언어만 안다면 할 수 있어.

speaker: SERVANT
raw: Ye say honestly, rest you merry!

sentences.en: You speak honestly.
sentences.ko: 정직하게 말씀하시네요.

sentences.en: Have a good day!
sentences.ko: 좋은 하루 되십시오!

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Stay, fellow; I can read.

sentences.en: Wait, friend; I can read.
sentences.ko: 잠깐, 이봐, 나 글 읽을 줄 알아.

raw: He reads the letter.

sentences.en: Romeo reads the letter.
sentences.ko: 로미오가 편지를 읽는다.

speaker: ROMEO

sentences.en: Mr. Martino and his wife and daughters.
sentences.ko: 마르티노 씨와 그의 아내 그리고 딸들.

sentences.en: Count Anselmo and his beautiful sisters.
sentences.ko: 안셀모 백작과 그의 아름다운 자매들.

sentences.en: The lady widow of Utruvio.
sentences.ko: 우트루비오의 과부 부인.

sentences.en: Mr. Placentio and his lovely nieces.
sentences.ko: 플라센티오 씨와 그의 사랑스러운 조카들.

sentences.en: Mercutio and his brother Valentine.
sentences.ko: 머큐쇼와 그의 형제 발렌타인.

sentences.en: My uncle Capulet, his wife, and daughters.
sentences.ko: 내 숙부 캐퓰릿과 그의 아내, 그리고 딸들.

sentences.en: My fair niece Rosaline and Livia.
sentences.ko: 나의 아름다운 조카 로잘린과 리비아.

sentences.en: Mr. Valentio and his cousin Tybalt.
sentences.ko: 발렌티오 씨와 그의 사촌 티볼트.

sentences.en: Lucio and the lively Helena.
sentences.ko: 루치오와 활기찬 헬레나.

sentences.en: A beautiful gathering.
sentences.ko: 아름다운 모임이군.

raw: Gives back the paper

sentences.en: Romeo gives back the paper.
sentences.ko: 로미오가 종이를 돌려준다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Whither should they come?

sentences.en: Where should they come to?
sentences.ko: 그들이 어디로 와야 하지?

speaker: SERVANT
raw: Up.

sentences.en: Up.
sentences.ko: 위로요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Whither to supper?

sentences.en: Where is the dinner?
sentences.ko: 어디로 저녁 먹으러 오라는 거지?

speaker: SERVANT
raw: To our house.

sentences.en: To our house.
sentences.ko: 저희 집으로요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Whose house?

sentences.en: Whose house?
sentences.ko: 누구의 집이지?

speaker: SERVANT
raw: My master’s.

sentences.en: My master's.
sentences.ko: 제 주인님의 댁입니다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Indeed I should have ask’d you that before.

sentences.en: I should have asked you that before.
sentences.ko: 그건 진작 물어봤어야 했는데.

speaker: SERVANT
raw:
Now I’ll tell you without asking. My master is the great rich Capulet,
and if you be not of the house of Montagues, I pray come and crush a
cup of wine. Rest you merry.

sentences.en: Now I will tell you without being asked.
sentences.ko: 이제 묻지 않으셔도 말씀드리겠습니다.

sentences.en: My master is the wealthy Capulet.
sentences.ko: 제 주인님은 부유한 캐퓰릿입니다.

sentences.en: If you are not from the house of Montagues, please come and drink a cup of wine.
sentences.ko: 몬태규 집안 사람이 아니시라면, 오셔서 포도주 한잔 드십시오.

sentences.en: Have a good day.
sentences.ko: 좋은 하루 되십시오.

raw: Exit.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
At this same ancient feast of Capulet’s
Sups the fair Rosaline whom thou so lov’st;
With all the admired beauties of Verona.
Go thither and with unattainted eye,
Compare her face with some that I shall show,
And I will make thee think thy swan a crow.

sentences.en: The beautiful Rosaline, whom you love so much, will eat at this same old feast of Capulet's.
sentences.ko: 네가 그토록 사랑하는 아름다운 로잘린도 바로 이 캐퓰릿의 잔치에 올 거야.

sentences.en: She will be there with all the famous beauties of Verona.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 베로나의 모든 유명한 미인들과 함께 그곳에 있을 거야.

sentences.en: Go there and look at her with fresh eyes.
sentences.ko: 거기 가서 새로운 눈으로 그녀를 바라봐 봐.

sentences.en: Compare her face with another face that I will show you.
sentences.ko: 내가 보여줄 다른 얼굴과 그녀의 얼굴을 비교해 보라고.

sentences.en: I will make you think your swan is a crow.
sentences.ko: 네 백조가 까마귀처럼 보이게 해 줄게.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
When the devout religion of mine eye
Maintains such falsehood, then turn tears to fire;
And these who, often drown’d, could never die,
Transparent heretics, be burnt for liars.
One fairer than my love? The all-seeing sun
Ne’er saw her match since first the world begun.

sentences.en: When the faith of my eyes believes such a lie, then let tears turn into fire.
sentences.ko: 내 눈이 그런 거짓말을 믿는다면, 눈물이 불꽃으로 변하게 해라.

sentences.en: My eyes have drowned in tears many times but never died.
sentences.ko: 내 눈은 여러 번 눈물에 잠겼지만 한 번도 죽지 않았다.

sentences.en: If they lie, let them be burned as liars.
sentences.ko: 거짓이라면 거짓말쟁이로 낙인찍혀 타버리게 하라.

sentences.en: Is there someone more beautiful than my love?
sentences.ko: 내 사랑보다 더 아름다운 사람이 또 있단 말이냐?

sentences.en: The all-seeing sun has never seen anyone equal to her since the world began.
sentences.ko: 모든 것을 보는 태양도 세상이 시작된 이후 그녀와 대등한 사람을 본 적이 없다.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Tut, you saw her fair, none else being by,
Herself pois’d with herself in either eye:
But in that crystal scales let there be weigh’d
Your lady’s love against some other maid
That I will show you shining at this feast,
And she shall scant show well that now shows best.

sentences.en: Well, you saw her beauty because no one else was around.
sentences.ko: 글쎄, 주변에 아무도 없었기에 그녀의 아름다움을 본 것뿐이야.

sentences.en: You only saw her in your own eyes.
sentences.ko: 넌 그녀를 너 혼자만의 눈으로 본 거야.

sentences.en: But let us weigh your lady's love on a crystal scale against another girl.
sentences.ko: 하지만 수정 저울에 네 연인과 다른 소녀를 달아 보자.

sentences.en: I will show you another girl who shines at this feast.
sentences.ko: 이 잔치에서 빛나는 또 다른 소녀를 보여줄게.

sentences.en: Then the girl who looks best to you now will hardly look good at all.
sentences.ko: 그러면 지금 네 눈에 가장 아름다워 보이는 그 소녀도 별로 예뻐 보이지 않을 거야.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I’ll go along, no such sight to be shown,
But to rejoice in splendour of my own.

sentences.en: I will go along.
sentences.ko: 함께 가겠어.

sentences.en: But not to see any such girl.
sentences.ko: 하지만 그런 여자를 보러 가는 건 아니야.

sentences.en: I will go only to enjoy the beauty of my own love.
sentences.ko: 나는 오직 내 사랑의 아름다움을 즐기기 위해 갈 뿐이야.

raw: Exeunt.
